bites.title: Choose the shot
bites.body: The camera decides what the final picture shows. Framing is half of every image.

bites.title: Look through it
bites.body: Hover the viewport and press 0 on the number pad. You're looking through the camera now.
bites.hint: No numpad? View menu, Cameras, Active Camera.

bites.title: Camera to view
bites.body: Middle-drag to orbit out of the camera, find an angle you love, then press Ctrl+Alt+Numpad 0. The camera jumps to exactly what you see.
bites.hint: No numpad? View menu, Align View, Align Active Camera to View.

bites.title: Change the lens
bites.body: Click the camera in the Outliner, open the green camera tab (Object Data), set Focal Length to 85. Long lenses flatten and flatter.

bites.title: Drive the camera
bites.body: Press N, open the View tab, and tick Lock Camera to View. Now orbiting in camera view moves the camera itself.
bites.hint: Sidebar (N), View tab, look for Lock Camera to View.

bites.title: Frame it, then unlock
bites.body: In camera view (numpad 0), orbit and pan until the cube sits nicely in the frame. Then untick Lock Camera to View.

bites.title: Blur the background
bites.body: Back in the camera's Object Data tab, tick Depth of Field, set Focus on Object to the Cube, and F-Stop to 1.4.

bites.title: Lesson 11: cleared
bites.body:
Camera view, camera to view, focal length, Lock Camera to View, and depth of field.

Scroll on for Lesson 12: take the picture.
